title: Organ Systems and Responses
subject: Science
source: NYSED 2025 Grade 8 ILS Released Items, Questions 19-23
directions: Base your answers to questions 19 through 23 on the information below and on your knowledge of science.

intro.html: On the field, a soccer player responds to stimuli in various ways. Coordinated responses are a result of the player’s body systems working together. These responses are intended to help the body maintain homeostasis or are learned behaviors performed by the player.

intro.caption: (Not drawn to scale)
intro.alt: Illustration of a soccer player kicking a ball. Lines connect the player to enlarged drawings of an eye, a heart, lungs, bone, and muscle, each labeled.

goalie.html: In soccer, when a shot is taken, the goalie from the opposing team tries to catch or block the shot in order to prevent the other team from scoring. This action involves a series of coordinated responses in the goalie’s body.

goalie.caption: Reaction to Incoming Ball
goalie.alt: Illustration of a goalie reaching for an incoming soccer ball, with dashed arrows and numbers 1 through 6 marking the path from the ball to the eyes, to the brain, down to the arms, and to the hands. A numbered key lists: 1. Ball approaches; 2. Eyes see ball; 3. Visual information sent to brain; 4. Brain processes information; 5. Response sent from brain to muscles; 6. Hands catch or block the ball.

gases.html: The model below represents the transport of gases within a muscle cell in a soccer player’s body. Structures labeled X are organelles within the muscle cell.

gases.caption: Model of Oxygen and Carbon Dioxide Transport
gases.alt: Model of gas transport. Blood travels from the heart to an air sac in a lung, where oxygen and carbon dioxide move across a blood vessel, then returns to the heart and on to the body cells in a muscle. An enlarged muscle cell shows blood vessels with red blood cells, oxygen moving into the cell, carbon dioxide moving out, and two organelles labeled X.

energy.html: The model below identifies the chemical formulas of some molecules in the cells of a soccer player. One molecule is missing.

energy.caption: Production of Energy Model
energy.alt: Model of a reaction. An empty box labeled Missing reactant, plus O2, with an arrow pointing to CO2, plus H2O, plus Energy.

body.html: While playing soccer, athletes often experience changes in body temperature. The model below represents the different ways the human body responds to changes in body temperature to maintain homeostasis.

body.caption: Body Response Model
body.alt: Cycle diagram around a human figure. Body temperature falls leads to a box listing: blood vessels constrict so that heat is conserved; sweat glands do not secrete fluid; shivering generates heat, which warms the body. That leads to Heat is retained, then Normal body temperature. Body temperature rises leads to a box listing: blood vessels dilate, resulting in heat loss to the environment; sweat glands secrete fluid; as the fluid evaporates, heat is lost from the body. That leads to Heat is lost to the environment, then Normal body temperature.

items.stem: The player’s coach always encourages all participants to work together as a team. The player claims that the human body works similarly because the body consists of interacting systems. Which piece of evidence supports this claim?
options: Cells in the human body contain a nuclei, cell membrane, and vacuoles.
Organs in the human body are composed of different types of tissue.
The mouth, stomach, and intestines are organs of the human digestive system.
The tissues of the muscular system move the human skeletal system.
